query: What happens if the grizzly fails or arch formation occurs in a track hopper?

text_chunks.title: The Track Hopper area looks quiet between unloadings. Is it safe to approach the grizzly edge?
text_chunks.content: The Track Hopper area looks quiet between unloadings. Is it safe to approach the grizzly edge? A Yes — if no wagon is on the track, it is safe B Yes — the feeder stops automatically between unloading cycles C No — feeder may still run, arch could collapse, bars may be wet, dust may be present underground D Yes, but only briefly and with both hands free

text_chunks.title: What is "arch formation" and why is it dangerous?
text_chunks.content: What is "arch formation" and why is it dangerous? A The hopper structure is arch-shaped for strength B A safety gate that closes the hopper outlet C Coal particles bridge the outlet, stopping flow — then collapse suddenly in a dangerous surge D Coal piling up above ground level during overfill

text_chunks.title: What happens if the grizzly fails?
text_chunks.content: What happens if the grizzly fails? 🚨 Chain of Destruction 🪨 Boulder/large lump — destroys feeder belt or apron chain completely 🔩 Metal debris (bolts, wire) — cuts conveyor belt downstream 🌿 Rope or wood — wraps around feeder shaft, causes jam and stall 🪨 Shale/stone — jams between apron plates, cracking the steel pans ⚠ Rule

text_chunks.title: What is the fundamental principle of a Track Hopper?
text_chunks.content: What is the fundamental principle of a Track Hopper? A The wagon is physically rotated to empty coal B Bottom doors open and coal falls by gravity into pit below C A vacuum system draws coal out of the wagon D Hydraulic rams tilt the wagon sideways

breadcrumb: What is the fundamental principle of a Track Hopper?

text_chunks.title: What is a Track Hopper?
text_chunks.content: What is a Track Hopper? COAL WAGON bottom doors open ⬇⬇⬇ coal accumulating Track Hopper Pit (underground) Rail wagon with open bottom doors discharging coal by gravity into underground hopper A Track Hopper is an underground pit built beneath a rail track. Wagons with bottom-opening doors drive over it — coal falls straight through into the pit below. No tipping. No rotation. Just gravity.

text_chunks.title: Arch Formation — The Silent Stop
text_chunks.content: Arch Formation — The Silent Stop Coal above arch ARCH (bridge) ⛔ Flow STOPS Coal above builds up · pressure increases Arch formation — coal bridges the outlet, all flow stops. Pressure above increases silently. 💧 More likely with wet, fine, or clay-rich coal ❄️ Increases in winter — moisture freezes, coal compacts ⏰ Static storage — coal that sits too long settles and bridges

text_chunks.title: Grizzly & Accumulation
text_chunks.content: Grizzly & Accumulation Every piece of coal gets size-classified here. Broken bars = unprotected feeder. Inspect after every unloading, never during. Tramp material on bars must be removed safely. The hopper buffers between variable wagon discharge rate and steady feeder rate. Overfill → coal at grizzly level (fall hazard). Underfill with arch → surge when it fails. Both extremes are dangerous.

text_chunks.title: Two cracked grizzly bars created a gap
text_chunks.content: Two cracked grizzly bars created a gap A 400 mm boulder passed through the gap → entered hopper → reached belt feeder → belt torn over 2 metres. Consequence Track hopper offline for 3 days Belt replacement + grizzly repair. Coal receipt suspended. Boiler load reduced. Emergency coal draw-down from yard. Consequence

text_chunks.title: The Grizzly — first line of defence
text_chunks.content: The Grizzly — first line of defence gap 200–300mm Fine coal ✓ passes LARGE LUMP ⛔ STOPPED GRIZZLY SCREEN — Top View ↓ Fine coal falls freely into hopper pit below Steel bar grid — small coal passes, oversized material and debris are stopped The Grizzly is a grid of thick steel bars (75–100 mm section) across the hopper opening. It is the only barrier between uncontrolled wagon contents and the precision-engineered machinery below.

text_chunks.title: 5 deceptive situations
text_chunks.content: 5 deceptive situations 😶 Empty, quiet grizzly → feeder still running below; void forming 😶 Coal level looks stable → arch formed; 80+ tonnes balanced above 😶 No wagons on track → wet coal left on grizzly bars; extreme slip risk 😶 Feeder belt appears stopped → motor energised; restarts without warning 😶 Area looks clean → coal dust suspended in underground gallery 🚨 The Rule
